A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bézier Splatting study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original rendering-time measurements, image-vectorization results, ablations, and DIV2K and Kodak comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds original comparisons with Adobe Image Trace and experiments varying rendering resolution and sampling density.

M1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies splitting an open curve when its middle opacity is more than 0.5 below both endpoints; v3 describes discarding such curves. This is a limited reported procedural change, although v4 retains the conflicting discard description in Section 3.5. The core sampling, rasterization, and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The DIV2K, Kodak, Clipart1K, and DanbooRegion coverage is retained. Appendix A adds a resolution-transfer scenario: rendering optimized representations at 4K and 8K relative to a 2K baseline.

E2.justification: v4 adds an evaluated conventional vectorization comparator, Adobe Illustrator Image Trace, in Table 5. The existing DiffVG, LIVE, and LIVSS comparison memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Adobe comparison uses five DIV2K images and approximately 20K parameters per method; the resolution experiment uses four images with original, doubled, and quadrupled sampling densities. Figure 3 changes its closed-curve example from 512 to 1,024 curves, although Section 4.2 still says 512. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds a sampling-density sensitivity analysis testing preservation of rendering quality at higher resolutions. The existing pruning, layer-wise optimization, curve-count, timing, and opacity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add Adobe-comparison and resolution results. Figure 1 revises open-curve forward/backward times from 13.2/24.5 ms to 4.6/4.8 ms. Figure 3 replaces the closed-curve example with a different image and curve budget, so its changed PSNRs are not comparable performance gains. Existing aggregate benchmark, ablation, and Kodak values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and the underlying mathematical formulations are unchanged. The added pseudocode documents procedures and implementation notation without introducing a substantive theoretical result, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The core claims about fast, high-fidelity rasterization, adaptive curve allocation, and SVG compatibility remain. One contribution bullet replaces explicit speedup factors with 'order-of-magnitude,' while the abstract and conclusion retain the original factors.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explanation connecting analytically derived Gaussian parameters and increased sampling density to preservation of quality at higher resolutions. It also interprets the Adobe comparison as supporting higher fidelity. The existing convexity and closed-curve computation limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds pruning/densification pseudocode and details including the Euclidean color-difference threshold of 0.03 and connected components of a quantized error map. The printed project-page address also changes. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained training settings.

R1.justification: v4 adds an Adobe Illustrator reference and limited positioning against conventional image vectorization. The earlier research citations and principal related-work discussion are retained after renumbering.

P1.justification: Changes include shortened section titles, removal of duplicated sampling prose, author/conference information, acknowledgments, and a new implementation appendix. Most existing paragraphs and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds two result tables and a pruning algorithm box, replaces Figure 3's closed-curve panel, and relocates Figure 2. The existing appendix illustrations remain the same, with tables and sections shifted or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons and pruning pseudocode broaden evidence and implementation detail, but introduce unresolved reporting problems. Table 6 omits its metric; the Adobe PSNR mean is stated as 24.904 although Table 5 averages 24.504; and Appendix B's splitting rule conflicts with Section 3.5's removal rule. These issues limit the added material's interpretability and reproducibility, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
